concepts.title: The last production-agent decision
concepts.research_question: For one production agent, who made the access, authority, funding, monitoring, incident, and shutdown decisions, using what evidence and with what measured outcome?
concepts.existing_evidence: BATCH-2026-010 identifies zero production role-at-source-time evidence and recommends a matched organizational case.
concepts.missing_evidence: Concrete decision rights, handoffs, denominators, outcomes, costs, failures, and time horizon.
concepts.ideal_executive_role: CISO, CIO, CTO, CFO, GC, CEO, business-unit owner, or board director with direct authority in the same deployment
concepts.ideal_experience_profile: Personally approved, changed, contained, funded, audited, or stopped a deployed agent in the last 18 months
concepts.industry_context: Regulated or high-consequence deployment; include finance, healthcare, critical infrastructure, public sector, and technology
concepts.geography_context: At least two regulatory regions; record speaker, organization, operating, incident, and regulatory geography separately
concepts.suggested_format: 45-minute recorded or attributable interview plus structured deployment worksheet
questions: What was the specific agent, task, autonomy level, and decision you personally made?
What could it access or delegate, and how was that authority represented?
Which other roles had approval, veto, budget, incident, or board-reporting authority?
What evidence, denominator, cost, and outcome changed the decision?
What failed, was abandoned, or remains unknown?
concepts.evidence_the_interview_could_add: Role-at-source-time testimony and a matched implementation case with traceable control and outcome fields.
concepts.rights_and_recording_requirements: Written consent for recording, transcription, attribution level, paraphrase, excerpts, indexing, corrections, and retention; no confidential architecture secrets.
concepts.conflict_considerations: Positive-case and vendor-selection bias; verify outcomes independently and recruit failed or abandoned cases.
concepts.success_criteria: One fully consented case with role at source time, exact locators, at least two roles interviewed, control denominator, outcome, limitation, and independent corroboration plan.

sponsorship.conflict_risk: Sponsor could favor its control framework or clients.
sponsorship.required_disclosure: Funding purpose and any client relationship to the case.
sponsorship.funding_findings_separation: Sponsor has no question, recruitment, analysis, or approval role.
sponsorship.data_access_limits: Public output only; no recordings, worksheets, identities, or row-level data.
sponsorship.publication_independence: OFF controls methods, findings, corrections, and release.

concepts.title: CISO: when agent access became the incident
concepts.research_question: How did a security leader detect, contain, investigate, and report an agent-access event?
concepts.existing_evidence: OFF’s public CISO report identifies agent access as a directional concern; the index has no verified CISO incident testimony.
concepts.missing_evidence: Inventory coverage, alert denominator, containment time, false positives, loss, recovery, budget, and board reporting.
concepts.ideal_executive_role: CISO or head of security at source time
concepts.ideal_experience_profile: Owned an agent-access incident, near miss, audit finding, or abandoned deployment
concepts.industry_context: Financial services, healthcare, critical infrastructure, retail, or enterprise software
concepts.geography_context: Multi-region sample with regulatory scope disclosed
concepts.suggested_format: Incident reconstruction interview with a publishable redacted timeline
questions: How was the agent inventoried?
What signal identified the event and what was the false-positive context?
How quickly were access and credentials revoked?
Who funded remediation and who was briefed?
What would you do differently?
concepts.evidence_the_interview_could_add: Security operator evidence on detection, revocation, containment, cost, and assurance.
concepts.rights_and_recording_requirements: Written consent; approve redactions; prohibit exploit detail that raises risk; exact attribution choice documented.
concepts.conflict_considerations: Legal privilege, reputation risk, insurer restrictions, and post-incident hindsight.
concepts.success_criteria: A rights-cleared timeline with denominators, containment metric, uncertainty, and corroborating artifact or second role.

sponsorship.suitable_sponsor_category: Cyber insurer or security professional association
sponsorship.conflict_risk: Sponsor may favor controls it underwrites or sells.
sponsorship.funding_findings_separation: No control ranking or sponsor-selected case.
sponsorship.publication_independence: Negative and inconclusive findings must remain publishable.

concepts.title: CIO: the agent identity operating model
concepts.research_question: How does enterprise IT integrate agent inventory, credential issuance, policy, lifecycle events, reliability, and service ownership?
concepts.existing_evidence: Candidate governance frameworks describe integrated controls; there is no verified CIO implementation evidence.
concepts.missing_evidence: Platform ownership, integration burden, availability tradeoffs, procurement, deprovisioning, and shared-service economics.
concepts.ideal_executive_role: CIO or enterprise-platform leader at source time
concepts.ideal_experience_profile: Operates a shared identity, integration, or AI platform supporting multiple business units
concepts.industry_context: Large enterprise with heterogeneous IAM and cloud environments
concepts.geography_context: North America, Europe, and Asia-Pacific cases
concepts.suggested_format: Architecture-and-operating-model interview with a non-sensitive responsibility map
questions: Which system is authoritative for agent inventory?
How are credentials issued, rotated, and retired?
Where do reliability and security requirements conflict?
Who pays for shared controls?
Which integration was abandoned and why?
concepts.evidence_the_interview_could_add: CIO role evidence on lifecycle operations, integration, reliability, procurement, and cost.
concepts.rights_and_recording_requirements: Consent for diagram, transcript, and indexed paraphrases; exclude confidential system identifiers.
concepts.success_criteria: A responsibility map plus at least one measured reliability, lifecycle, or cost outcome.

sponsorship.conflict_risk: Platform framing could privilege one ecosystem.
sponsorship.data_access_limits: No architecture worksheet or participant identity access.

concepts.title: CTO: identity granularity and delegation
concepts.research_question: When should an agent, instance, session, task, or subagent receive a distinct identity and attenuated authority?
concepts.existing_evidence: Candidate propositions support distinguishable identities and attenuated delegation but do not compare designs.
concepts.missing_evidence: Developer constraints, interoperability, performance, privacy, failure modes, and task-utility tradeoffs.
concepts.ideal_executive_role: CTO, chief architect, or AI platform engineering leader at source time
concepts.ideal_experience_profile: Shipped a multi-agent or tool-using system with production authorization controls
concepts.industry_context: Enterprise software, fintech, healthcare technology, or cloud platform
concepts.geography_context: Cross-region technical cases with deployment market disclosed
concepts.suggested_format: Technical executive interview plus four-pattern design comparison
questions: What is the identity unit and why?
How does authority change across delegation?
What breaks if identities are more granular?
How are spawned agents discovered and stopped?
Which evidence would change the architecture?
concepts.evidence_the_interview_could_add: Comparable design rationales, constraints, and outcomes for identity granularity and delegation.
concepts.rights_and_recording_requirements: Rights-cleared diagrams and code-free descriptions; no secrets or exploitable configuration.
concepts.conflict_considerations: Architecture advocacy and vendor protocol interests.
concepts.success_criteria: A comparison with explicit context, tradeoffs, observed failure, and no universal-design claim.

sponsorship.conflict_risk: Sponsor may promote its protocol as the answer.
sponsorship.publication_independence: Competing designs and failures must be retained.

concepts.title: CFO: the control investment gate
concepts.research_question: How does finance decide whether agent-identity controls merit a dedicated line, shared platform allocation, insurance treatment, or deployment delay?
concepts.existing_evidence: OFF’s public CISO report describes a directional governance-budget gap; the index has zero verified CFO evidence.
concepts.missing_evidence: Cost model, loss estimate, ROI horizon, budget owner, insurance, procurement gate, and post-implementation benefit.
concepts.ideal_executive_role: CFO, chief accounting officer, finance transformation leader, or risk-finance executive at source time
concepts.ideal_experience_profile: Approved or rejected an AI governance, IAM, security, or agent-platform investment
concepts.geography_context: At least two accounting and regulatory contexts
questions: What business decision triggered the spend?
Which loss or value denominator was used?
Who owned and benefited from the control?
What evidence cleared or failed the gate?
How was success measured after funding?
concepts.evidence_the_interview_could_add: Finance role evidence on budgets, control economics, decision horizons, and outcome measurement.
concepts.rights_and_recording_requirements: Consent with financial redaction rules; figures published only with denominator and approval.
concepts.conflict_considerations: Commercial sensitivity, survivorship, and post-hoc ROI construction.
concepts.success_criteria: A decision pathway with cost range or normalized denominator, time horizon, owner, and measured or explicitly unknown result.

sponsorship.suitable_sponsor_category: Bank, insurer, or finance professional association
sponsorship.conflict_risk: Sponsor may benefit from a new budget category.
sponsorship.funding_findings_separation: No sponsor access to instrument or analysis.
sponsorship.data_access_limits: Aggregate public output; no company-level financial data.
sponsorship.publication_independence: Unfunded and rejected cases remain publishable.

concepts.title: General counsel: traceability without overreach
concepts.research_question: What evidence must connect an agent action to accountable entities while preserving privacy, privilege, lawful anonymity, and proportional retention?
concepts.existing_evidence: Candidate governance sources call for principal traceability and human legal-entity accountability; no verified legal counterposition exists.
concepts.missing_evidence: Jurisdiction-specific duties, contracting, evidentiary sufficiency, retention limits, privilege, and investigated cases.
concepts.ideal_executive_role: General counsel, chief privacy officer, or senior product counsel at source time
concepts.ideal_experience_profile: Reviewed a deployed agent, incident, regulator inquiry, or contractual allocation of agent risk
concepts.industry_context: Financial services, healthcare, employment, public sector, or consumer platforms
concepts.geography_context: EU/EEA, UK, United States, and Asia-Pacific legal contexts
questions: Which action record is legally necessary?
Who can be the accountable entity?
What should not be retained or deanonymized?
How are developer, deployer, user, platform, and tool provider obligations allocated?
Which uncertainty blocks deployment?
concepts.evidence_the_interview_could_add: Legal role evidence and bounded counterpositions on traceability, anonymity, retention, and responsibility.
concepts.rights_and_recording_requirements: No legal advice claim; written attribution approval; exclude privileged or client-identifying facts.
concepts.conflict_considerations: Jurisdictional overgeneralization and law-firm business development.
concepts.success_criteria: At least one scoped legal rule, one uncertainty, one privacy limit, and one implementation implication with jurisdiction stated.

sponsorship.suitable_sponsor_category: Neutral legal or privacy professional association
sponsorship.conflict_risk: Professional advice may be mistaken for settled law.
sponsorship.required_disclosure: Jurisdiction, client-development interest, and non-advice status.
sponsorship.funding_findings_separation: Independent editorial and competing legal views.

concepts.title: Board director: what assurance is enough?
concepts.research_question: What agent-governance evidence does a board need to set risk appetite and oversee management without operating the controls?
concepts.existing_evidence: The repository identifies zero board role evidence; OFF operates a public-board dinner format and public community page.
concepts.missing_evidence: Materiality, inventory confidence, incident thresholds, assurance source, reporting cadence, accountability, and decision use.
concepts.ideal_executive_role: Public-company board director or committee chair at source time
concepts.ideal_experience_profile: Audit, risk, technology, or cybersecurity oversight involving deployed AI
concepts.industry_context: Public companies in regulated and technology-intensive sectors
concepts.geography_context: Board-governance regimes disclosed; no universal board rule inferred
concepts.suggested_format: Attributable board-governance interview or anonymized research interview with separate consent
questions: What agent inventory number would you trust?
Which risks are material enough for board reporting?
Who should attest to controls?
What action did a board report change?
Where would more reporting create noise rather than oversight?
concepts.evidence_the_interview_could_add: Board role evidence on assurance, materiality, cadence, and governance use.
concepts.rights_and_recording_requirements: Separate event and research consent; no board materials, attendee list, or company confidential information.
concepts.conflict_considerations: Board confidentiality, fiduciary context, and reputational signaling.
concepts.success_criteria: A scoped assurance framework tied to an actual oversight decision and explicit limitations.

sponsorship.conflict_risk: Sponsor framework may be presented as accepted practice.
sponsorship.funding_findings_separation: No sponsor-selected directors or prescribed conclusion.
sponsorship.data_access_limits: No identities, board materials, or private notes.

concepts.title: Business-unit owner: the shadow deployment
concepts.research_question: How does an agent enter a workflow outside central inventory, and what happens when platform, security, finance, and legal controls catch up?
concepts.existing_evidence: OFF public research describes business-unit buying and shadow AI directionally; no indexed operator case verifies the path.
concepts.missing_evidence: Purchase route, access grant, data use, value, discovery, remediation, and ownership handoff.
concepts.ideal_executive_role: Business-unit president, COO, CMO, CRO, or functional transformation leader at source time
concepts.ideal_experience_profile: Sponsored or inherited a tool-using agent outside a central AI program
concepts.industry_context: Marketing, sales, finance, customer operations, or supply chain
concepts.geography_context: Operating and data-regulatory geography recorded separately
concepts.suggested_format: Workflow journey interview with decision and control timeline
questions: What problem justified adoption?
Who granted system and data access?
When did central functions learn of it?
What value and risk were measured?
Was the workflow retained, constrained, or stopped?
concepts.evidence_the_interview_could_add: Buyer-side evidence on adoption, value, shadow inventory, and cross-functional handoffs.
concepts.rights_and_recording_requirements: Consent for workflow description and redaction; no employee surveillance or customer data.
concepts.conflict_considerations: Normalization of policy bypass and selective success stories.
concepts.success_criteria: A documented route from adoption to control with outcome, handoff, and failure or burden disclosed.

sponsorship.conflict_risk: Sponsor may promote faster adoption over control.
sponsorship.publication_independence: No product promotion or lead sharing.

concepts.title: Agent shutdown and decommissioning failure
concepts.research_question: What remains after an agent is stopped, and how are identities, credentials, integrations, data, subagents, and audit duties retired?
concepts.existing_evidence: Candidate lifecycle propositions recommend revocation and deprovisioning; there is no comparative production outcome.
concepts.missing_evidence: Orphaned access prevalence in the observed case, revocation latency, residual data, task failure, cost, and recovery.
concepts.ideal_executive_role: CIO, CISO, CTO, platform owner, or internal-audit leader at source time
concepts.ideal_experience_profile: Decommissioned, canceled, or rolled back an agent deployment
concepts.geography_context: Any region with retention and deletion requirements disclosed
questions: What triggered shutdown?
Which identities and credentials existed?
How was completeness tested?
What remained after the first pass?
What did retirement cost and how long did it take?
concepts.evidence_the_interview_could_add: Rare negative-case evidence on lifecycle completeness and residual risk.
concepts.rights_and_recording_requirements: Strong redaction and incident-safety review; explicit permission for failure publication.
concepts.conflict_considerations: High nonresponse, legal sensitivity, and blame avoidance.
concepts.success_criteria: A failed or abandoned case with a retirement checklist, measured latency or residue, and limitation statement.

sponsorship.conflict_risk: Sponsor may minimize cases involving its tools.
sponsorship.data_access_limits: No raw postmortem or company identity without consent.

concepts.title: Privacy engineer or civil-society counterposition
concepts.research_question: Where can agent traceability become unnecessary surveillance, forced identification, or over-retention?
concepts.existing_evidence: Current staging propositions emphasize traceability; the dossier gap explicitly lacks privacy, anonymity, surveillance, and over-control counterpositions.
concepts.missing_evidence: Concrete harms, alternative designs, proportionality tests, lawful anonymity, and affected-user perspective.
concepts.ideal_executive_role: Chief privacy officer, senior privacy engineer, civil-society policy leader, or regulator at source time
concepts.ideal_experience_profile: Designed or challenged identity and audit controls for high-scale automated systems
concepts.industry_context: Consumer platforms, public services, employment, healthcare, or financial inclusion
concepts.geography_context: EU/EEA plus one non-European privacy or civil-rights context
concepts.suggested_format: Counterposition interview with a design-alternative worksheet
questions: Which actor actually needs to be identifiable?
What harm follows from persistent linkage?
When is pseudonymity sufficient?
What data should expire?
What implementation preserves accountability with less surveillance?
concepts.evidence_the_interview_could_add: Credible challenge and alternative designs for traceability, audit, and accountability claims.
concepts.rights_and_recording_requirements: Public-source consent; protect affected individuals and avoid sensitive-trait inference.
concepts.conflict_considerations: Advocacy position must remain attributed and not be flattened into legal fact.
concepts.success_criteria: At least one well-scoped counterposition, one alternative control, and one evidence need.

sponsorship.conflict_risk: Advocacy funder may favor one policy outcome.
sponsorship.funding_findings_separation: Include legal, operator, and opposing views.

concepts.title: Regional operator and regulator pair
concepts.research_question: How do local law, infrastructure, procurement, and operating practice change agent identity and authority controls?
concepts.existing_evidence: BATCH-2026-011 found zero production regional evidence and a policy-heavy discovery queue.
concepts.missing_evidence: Locally grounded operator implementation connected to regulator or public-policy requirements.
concepts.ideal_executive_role: Local CISO, CIO, GC, public-sector technology leader, or regulator at source time
concepts.ideal_experience_profile: Implemented or supervised agent controls in the jurisdiction discussed
concepts.industry_context: Finance, healthcare, critical infrastructure, public administration, or technology
concepts.geography_context: First waves: Singapore or Japan, Europe, then Africa, Latin America and Caribbean, and Middle East and North Africa
concepts.suggested_format: Two linked interviews in the original language where necessary
questions: Which local rule or operating condition changed the design?
What is required versus chosen?
Which control failed locally?
How does evidence reach the regulator or board?
What should not be generalized outside this jurisdiction?
concepts.evidence_the_interview_could_add: Region-specific role evidence with explicit legal, operating, and language context.
concepts.rights_and_recording_requirements: Qualified language review, original-language transcript, translation approval, and no machine-only quotations.
concepts.conflict_considerations: Policy authority is not implementation effectiveness; local elites may not represent smaller firms.
concepts.success_criteria: One regulator and one operator source with verified roles, jurisdiction, original-language locator, translation review, and scoped comparison.

sponsorship.suitable_sponsor_category: Regional professional association or neutral foundation
sponsorship.conflict_risk: Sponsor may favor national or sector promotion.
sponsorship.funding_findings_separation: Local reviewers validate language, not conclusions.
sponsorship.data_access_limits: No participant contacts or private translations.

concepts.title: Benchmark author and deploying operator validity check
concepts.research_question: Which benchmark results informed deployment, and did they predict observed incidents, control effectiveness, or task utility?
concepts.existing_evidence: Candidate synthetic studies demonstrate bounded capabilities and tradeoffs but do not estimate production prevalence or guarantee deployment performance.
concepts.missing_evidence: Linked benchmark, model/version, deployment, incident, control, and outcome data.
concepts.ideal_executive_role: CISO, CTO, AI evaluation leader, or model-risk executive at source time
concepts.ideal_experience_profile: Used an agent-security benchmark in a production selection or control decision
concepts.geography_context: Deployment geography recorded; benchmark itself may have no human geography
questions: Which benchmark and version were used?
What decision did it affect?
Which deployment conditions differed?
What production outcomes agreed or diverged?
What would make the benchmark more decision-useful?
concepts.evidence_the_interview_could_add: A linked validity case connecting synthetic metrics to a bounded deployment decision.
concepts.rights_and_recording_requirements: Versioned benchmark citation, consent, and safe incident abstraction.
concepts.conflict_considerations: Benchmark-author reputation and vendor model interests.
concepts.success_criteria: A versioned benchmark-to-decision chain with convergent or divergent outcome and explicit external-validity limit.

sponsorship.conflict_risk: Vendor or benchmark sponsor could favor favorable validity results.
sponsorship.required_disclosure: Model, benchmark, funding, and author relationships.
sponsorship.data_access_limits: No incident-level raw data to sponsor.
sponsorship.publication_independence: Null and adverse validity findings remain publishable.
